title: A finite purely inseparable extension descends along a field extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields ($L$ a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension]) and let $B$ be a commutative $K$-algebra. Regard $L\otimes_KB$ as an $L$-algebra via $l\mapsto l\otimes1$. If $L\otimes_KB$ is a field and, via this map, a finite purely inseparable field extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], then $B$ is a field, the structure map $K\to B$ makes $B$ a finite purely inseparable field extension of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)$.

source.place: Implicit in the proof of Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202), where $k_i'$ is asserted to be a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k_i$ without argument; definition of purely inseparable: Fields, Definition Tag 09HE (fields.tex). Intended argument (agent): choose a $K$-basis of $L$ containing $1$ and a $K$-basis $(b_\lambda)$ of $B$ containing $1$; then $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ is an $L$-basis of $L\otimes_KB$, so $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)<\infty$, and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ is injective; hence $B$ is a domain finite over $K$, so a field; if $\beta\in B$ has $(1\otimes\beta)^q=l\otimes1$ ($q$ a power of the characteristic exponent), comparing coordinates in the basis $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ gives $\beta^q\in K$; in characteristic $0$, $\dim=1$ gives $B=K$.
